reason: The primary suffering described in this passage—the enslavement of the Israelites in Egypt—was not caused by their own fault. The text clearly indicates that the Egyptians enslaved them due to Pharaoh's fear of their growing numbers and his own hardness of heart (Exodus 1:8-14). While the Israelites do complain and show lack of faith during their wilderness journey (e.g., at Marah, Rephidim regarding water), these later trials are distinct from their initial enslavement. The enslavement itself was an external oppression imposed upon them, not a consequence of their own wrongdoing. God explicitly sends Moses to deliver them from this unjust captivity.
